name: OMAD / 36-hour fasts
lead: OMAD (one meal a day) is a form of time-restricted eating in which all daily food is eaten in a window of one to two hours; 36-hour fasts extend the pause between meals beyond a day.[1] Both are used in looksmaxxing communities to lose body fat quickly and get a leaner face.

Encyclopedic sources report that evidence for intermittent fasting matching calorie restriction is limited, with most human studies showing weight loss of about 2.5 to 9.9 percent.[1] Health bodies including the American Heart Association and the US National Institute on Aging have described the evidence as limited or inconclusive.[1]
infobox: Typical weight loss in studies (IF generally)

paras: OMAD is classed as a subtype of time-restricted eating, alongside 8 to 12 hour windows, alternate-day fasting and the 5:2 diet.[1] Fasts longer than 24 hours with only water are called periodic or extended fasts.[1][2]

Forum users report using OMAD alongside low-carbohydrate eating or weight-loss medication to reduce fat before a muscle-building phase, and ask whether to choose OMAD or longer water fasts.[3] Other users ask whether OMAD causes hair loss at a daily intake of about 1,500 calories, with one reply saying extreme deficits can cause shedding but that this intake probably would not.[4] Threads also discuss OMAD for morning bloating and growth hormone, with replies varying.

Weight loss from intermittent fasting includes fat and some lean mass; for time-restricted eating the fat-to-lean ratio is about 4:1.[1] Umbrella reviews in 2021 and 2024 reported improved weight and cardiometabolic outcomes in overweight or obese adults, with a smaller blood-pressure effect than continuous calorie restriction.[1] A 2026 review in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition discussed impacts, mechanisms and cautions of intermittent fasting.[5]

The American Heart Association said there was no good evidence of heart-health benefit, and the National Institute on Aging did not recommend such diets for the general public.[1] Fasting is not recommended for pregnant or breastfeeding women, children, older adults or people with or vulnerable to eating disorders.[1]

Reported effects include hunger, irritability, dizziness, nausea, headaches and impaired thinking, which one source says fade within a month; a systematic review reported no major adverse effects.[1] Dropout rates ranged from 2 to 38 percent.[1] Fasting is also reported to raise gallstone risk.[2]

Trials have examined time-restricted eating and alternate-day fasting rather than OMAD or 36-hour fasts specifically. A 2018 pilot study of 23 obese adults eating within an 8-hour window reported reduced body weight.[6] No studies found on OMAD or 36-hour fasts for facial appearance.

lore.intro: Forum threads discuss OMAD as a way to cut fat and manage hunger, often combined with low-carbohydrate eating.[3][4]

claims.claim: OMAD with low carbohydrate is a fast way to get lean
claims.believers: A user preparing for a muscle-building phase asks about OMAD versus water fasting, and a reply recommends a no-carbohydrate, high-fat, high-protein OMAD.[3]
claims.experts: Reviews report that intermittent fasting produces weight loss comparable to calorie restriction in some studies, with limited evidence overall; no studies found on OMAD combined with low carbohydrate for appearance.[1]

claims.claim: OMAD at about 1,500 calories does not cause hair loss
claims.believers: A forum reply says extreme deficits cause hair loss but 1,500 kcal probably would not.[4]
claims.experts: No published studies found in the sources reviewed have examined OMAD and hair loss.[1]

card.summary: One meal a day or 36-hour fasts for fast fat loss; intermittent fasting has modest evidence and health bodies call it inconclusive.
card.note: Not recommended for pregnancy, children, older adults or people prone to eating disorders; some lean mass is lost.

quick.overview:
OMAD packs all eating into one meal; 36-hour fasts leave a day and a half between meals. Forum users use them to cut fat and sometimes to reduce bloating.

Reviews show intermittent fasting can produce weight loss similar to calorie restriction in some studies, but health bodies describe the evidence as limited.
quick.mechanism: The pattern mainly lowers calorie intake. Weight lost includes fat and some lean mass.
quick.risks: Reported effects include hunger, dizziness, headaches and irritability. Fasting is not recommended for several groups, and prolonged fasts raise gallstone risk.
